paradigms.evidence: The Divine Liturgy, Axion estin: feminine accusative singular ἀειμακάριστον confirms the two-termination adjective; retain its regular lookup paradigm.
The Divine Liturgy, Axion estin: παναμώμητον is the feminine accusative of the two-termination compound παν- + ἀμώμητος. The suffix and accent class remain those of ἀμώμητος.

Strabo, Geography 14.1.14, attests πινακοθήκη and nominative plural πινακοθῆκαι. Derive the regular first-declension eta paradigm, including dative singular -ῃ and genitive plural -ῶν; the attested plural confirms the circumflex before short final -αι.

The funeral service, second stasis, attests κατετέθης in the hymn beginning Ὁ θάνατός σου Κύριε. Derive the passive aorist indicative from the attested accented stem with endings -ην, -ης, -η, -ημεν, -ητε, -ησαν.
Paschal canon, Ode 1: Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα λαμπρυνθῶμεν λαοί. The attested passive aorist stem takes the contracted subjunctive endings.

Menaion, March 20, Ode 7, attests ἀνθοπλίσαντες in the hymn beginning Ὅλον πρὸς σὲ μεταθέντες. Derive the regular active aorist participle from ἀνθοπλίσ-; long endings move the acute from the antepenult to the penult.

Archimedes, Arenarius 1, Mugler volume 2 (1971), page 137 line 22: ἀποχρὴ δέ μοι ἐς τὰν ἀπόδειξιν τοῦ προκειμένου γωνίαν λαβεῖν. The edited First1KGreek witness prints the contextual grave. Retain this exact Doric third-person singular present spelling under the independently defined impersonal head ἀπόχρη; the exporter supplies its citation acute without changing valid source citation accents globally.
paradigms.citation: Archimedes, Arenarius 1; Charles Mugler, Archimède volume 2 (1971), page 137 line 22

paradigms.evidence: Plato, Philebus 21b, attests δέοι’ before ἄν. This is elided second-person singular middle optative δέοιο; preserve the exact printed spelling rather than treating its apostrophe as a quotation mark.
Homer, Iliad 3.382, attests εἷσ’ before ἐν in the account of Aphrodite placing Paris in his chamber. Preserve this exact elided aorist reading independently of quotation punctuation.
Xenophanes, the fragment beginning Πάντα θεοῖσ’ ἀνέθηκαν, attests elided dative plural θεοῖσι before ἀνέθηκαν. Preserve the exact elision from this independent verse.
Hesiod, fragment 204.90, attests νίκησ’ before οὐδέ in the account of Helen's suitors. Preserve this genuine elided aorist spelling independently of punctuation-bearing Diorisis readings.

Menander, Sentences 290, prints πανταχοῦ’ στι. The apostrophe records prodelision of following ἐστί, not removal of a vowel from πανταχοῦ. Preserve the independently printed token spelling without generating other prodelision forms.
Athenaeus, Deipnosophistae 3.85, page 117b, attests παῖ’ before ἐκεῖνον. Preserve the genuine elided imperative παῖε; an independently complete noun παῖ followed by a quote is a separate reading.
Aristophanes, Lysistrata 1086, prints ποῦ’ στιν. The apostrophe represents prodelision of following ἐστίν, not elision of the interrogative's vowel. Preserve this exact printed token spelling only.
Homer, Odyssey 9.302, attests χείρ’ before ἐπιμασσάμενος. Preserve this genuine elided dative χειρί independently of complete nominatives accompanied by quotation punctuation.

Euripides, Heracles 954, attests ἐς ἀνδρῶν’ ἐσπεσών. This is genuine elision of accusative ἀνδρῶνα, the men's hall; it is distinct from a complete genitive plural ἀνδρῶν followed by quotation punctuation.

Homeric Hymn to Apollo 223, attests βῆς ἄν’ ὄρος. Preserve the genuine elided preposition ἀνά, with its elision accent, independently of a complete particle ἄν followed by quotation punctuation. The corpus noun/dative annotation does not determine this owner.
Plato, Symposium 174b, attests Ἀγάθων’ before ἐπί. Preserve the exact elision of accusative Ἀγάθωνα in the proverb, independently of complete nominatives followed by quotation punctuation.
Euripides, Orestes 591, attests Ἀπόλλων’ before ὅς as the object of ὁρᾷς. Preserve the genuine elision of accusative Ἀπόλλωνα, independently of complete nominatives followed by quotation punctuation.
Plutarch, Moralia 1010e, quotes ἔνι’ before οὐδέ. Preserve the genuine elision of neuter plural ἔνια independently of quotation punctuation attached to a complete ἔνι.
Aristophanes, Lysistrata 1037, attests ὥρασ’ before ἵκοισθ’. Herodian, Prosodia Catholica 1.501, explicitly discusses this quotation under the adverb ὥρασι. Preserve its exact genuine elision.

Euripides, Medea 1242, attests εἶ’ before ὁπλίζου. Ten independent edited corpus loci support this genuine elision of the interjection εἶα; preserve the exact spelling separately from audited quotation readings.
Euripides, Fragmenta 781.2, Nauck 1889, attests ἀνίησ’ before ἀτμόν. Preserve the genuine elision of ἀνίησι independently of punctuation-bearing Diorisis readings.
The Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, Cherubic Hymn, printed pages 14-15, attests εἰκονίζοντες. Admit this exact active present participle only.
Herodotus, Histories 6.133.2, uses the accusative plural ethnic name as the object of ἐπολιόρκεε. Preserve this exact proper-name form independently of the common-word lookup assignment.
Plato, Gorgias 467b, addresses Polus with the vocative Πῶλε. Preserve the attested name form rather than assigning its ownership only to the common noun πῶλος.
Titus 3.12 in the Westcott-Hort text spells the personal name Τύχικον. Other editions use Τυχικόν; retain both accent traditions instead of treating either as a common adjective.

Jude 1.11 in the received-text tradition has the indeclinable name Κορὲ after τοῦ. Other editions have Κόρε. The contextual grave is normalized to acute in the source specification and the exporter supplies its grave twin.

Nehemiah 13.28 spells the indeclinable personal name Ἰωαδὰ after υἱῶν. Keep the complete name rather than substituting the unrelated shorter name Ἰώδα. The contextual grave is normalized to acute and regenerated by the exporter.

Colossians 4.9 uses the personal name Ὀνησίμῳ as the dative complement of σύν. The SBL Greek New Testament identifies its lemma as Ὀνήσιμος; the independent GLAUx reading agrees. Keep this exact name form despite the flattened lookup assigning it to the common adjective ὀνήσιμος.

LSJ9 s.v. παῖσι explicitly records old Attic dative plural of παῖς. Retain only the dictionary-listed exact spelling under παῖς. The Basil OCR occurrences do not support its frequency; the separate Aeolic πᾶς interpretation is not used for this owner.
